title: Best AI Mobile App Builders 2026: Native vs Web Apps, Ranked
summary: Best free AI mobile app builder? 14 tools sorted by native iOS and Android publishing, free tiers, code export, and store fees, verified September 2026.
body_markdown:
In August 1994, IBM and BellSouth started selling a $899 handheld called Simon. It had a touchscreen, a stylus, an address book, and something no phone had shipped before: a way to run add-on software from a PCMCIA card. Simon sold about 50,000 units in six months before a one-hour battery and the appeal of slim flip phones ended it. There was no app store, no developer program, and no review queue. You wrote software for it or you didn't.


IBM Simon at the Computer History Museum. Photo: Michael Hicks via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0.


In 2026, a text prompt can produce that add-on software in minutes, and the thing that actually gates whether a stranger can install it on their phone hasn't changed since 2008: a store review queue, a developer account, and an annual fee.


That gate is where most "best AI mobile app builder" roundups get vague. Some tools generate a *mobile-web app* and call it done. Others generate native code and quietly move App Store submission to a paid plan. Few pages tell you which is which before you build.


> **TL;DR:** We sorted **14 AI mobile app builders** by what they publish: a **native** app for the App Store or Google Play (FlutterFlow, Rork, Draftbit, Adalo), or a **mobile-web app** on a shareable URL with no store review (Taskade Genesis, Glide, AppSheet). Free tiers, code export, and store fees verified September 2026.[Build a free mobile-web app →](https://www.taskade.com/create?entry_kind=content&source=blog&entry=%2Fblog%2Fai-mobile-app-builders)


---


## Quick Answer: The Best AI Mobile App Builder by What You Want


**The best AI mobile app builder depends on whether you need a native store binary or a working mobile-web app today.** For a Flutter project on both stores,[FlutterFlow](https://flutterflow.io/) leads. For AI-written native Swift,[Rork](https://rork.com/) is the most literal option. For a database-backed app with an AI agent and no store review,[Taskade Genesis](https://www.taskade.com/create?entry_kind=content&source=blog&entry=%2Fblog%2Fai-mobile-app-builders) is the fastest.

## What Is an AI Mobile App Builder, and Why "Free" Rarely Reaches the Store


**An AI mobile app builder turns a written description into an app that runs on a phone, but "runs on a phone" means three different things in 2026.** Some tools compile a real native binary — an IPA for iOS or an APK/AAB for Android — that you submit to Apple or Google for review. Some generate Flutter or React Native source that becomes native only after you run a build pipeline. Some skip the store and publish a mobile-responsive web app to a URL. Comparisons that blend all three make a free tier look more generous than it is.


```text

Bravo Studio, Rork, Replit (iOS)

Draftbit, Vibecode Pro, a0.dev,    (Xcode, EAS, Android Studio)     you submit it
Bolt + Expo (code only)            yourself
A mobile-web app                     Open a URL in the phone's        No review, no
Taskade Genesis, Glide, AppSheet,  browser; add to home screen      developer account
Base44                             for an app-like icon


```

## What Publishing to the App Store and Google Play Actually Costs


**Two fees apply no matter which AI builder you use, and almost no comparison adds them to the sticker price.**[Apple's Developer Program](https://developer.apple.com/support/enrollment/) is $99 a year, charged every year the app stays live.[Google Play's developer registration](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/6112435) is a one-time $25. Both accounts belong to you, not the builder, and both sit on top of whatever the AI tool charges.


Cost Amount When it hits Charged by


Apple Developer Program $99/year Every year the app stays listed Apple, not the AI tool


Google Play Console registration $25 one-time Once, before your first Android app ships Google, not the AI tool


Entry paid tier to unlock native export or store publishing $12–$200/month, see the table above On top of both store fees The AI app builder


Review-time risk Apple: 90% of submissions reviewed in under 24 hours on average. Google: up to 7 days or longer for some apps, plus a 14-day, 12-tester closed test for a new personal account Every submission and every update Unpaid time, on no pricing page


Review time is the cost that catches first-time publishers hardest, and no pricing page lists it. The2026 changes table and thelaunch card below carry Apple's and Google's own numbers.

## The Path From Prompt to a Live App


**Every mobile app, generated or hand-coded, crosses the same fork, and the fork happens earlier than most people plan for.**


The two branches diverge hard at step 3. Accounts, review, rejection, and resubmission belong to the native path alone. The web path's step 8 is "republish," not "resubmit."


The native branch also has more parties in it than first-time builders expect:

## How We Compared These Tools

- **Tools are split by what they publish** : native binary, exportable source, or mobile-web app.
- **We did not run one identical prompt through all 14 tools.** Several gate generation behind a paid plan, so a fair free-tier bake-off would mix free and paid output.
- **Taskade appears last** , in the mobile-web category, because that is honestly where it fits. Store fees and review times are listed separately, because they apply to every native builder equally.

## Native and Cross-Platform App Builders


These tools compile, or export code toward, a real binary you submit to the App Store or Google Play.


### 1.[FlutterFlow](https://flutterflow.io/) : Best for Exportable Flutter Code Across iOS, Android, and Web


[FlutterFlow](https://flutterflow.io/) is a visual builder that generates real Flutter code, then adds AI generation for screens, components, and full flows from a prompt or a Figma import. Because the output is standard Flutter, one codebase targets iOS, Android, and web.


FlutterFlow homepage, captured September 2026.


**Key features:** visual builder plus AI generation; Firebase and Supabase integration; in-browser preview; web publishing to FlutterFlow subdomains; a large template library.


**Free plan (verified Sep 23, 2026):** 2 projects and web publishing to 2 subdomains. AI assistance is capped at 5 requests for the lifetime of the account, not a monthly allowance. Code and APK download require a paid plan.


**Pros:**


- Real Flutter source, so a serious cross-platform app can start here and never leave
- One codebase reaches iOS, Android, and web
- The most established name across independent comparisons in this category


**Cons:**


- 5 lifetime AI requests makes the AI features close to a demo on free
- No code or APK export until Basic, which is the entire reason to pick Flutter
- Native publishing is not available at $0


**Pricing:** Basic $39/month for code export, APK download, and app store deployment.


**Bottom line:** the safest default if you want a real cross-platform app you can take anywhere, once you're paying.


### 2.[Rork](https://rork.com/) : Best for AI-Generated Native Swift, Kotlin, and React Native Apps


[Rork](https://rork.com/) generates mobile apps from a prompt in two modes: a free Design mode that proposes screens, and a paid Build mode that turns them into apps you can test on a device and publish. On Pro, Build mode writes SwiftUI for iPhone and Kotlin for Android. Rork Max adds iPad, Apple Watch, and Vision Pro.


Rork homepage, captured September 2026.


**Key features:** prompt-to-design in two stages; native SwiftUI and Kotlin output; Dev mode for code editing on paid plans.


**Free plan (re-checked Sep 24, 2026, per[Rork's own subscription docs](https://docs.rork.com/introduction/subscriptions) ):** 5 design credits a day, 35 a month in major markets, Design mode only. Build mode, publishing, and Dev mode all require a paid plan.


**Pros:**


- The most literal "AI writes native Swift" option we verified
- Rork Max reaches beyond phones to Watch and Vision Pro
- Design mode is a genuinely free way to see screens before paying


**Cons:**


- Free plan cannot build or publish anything, only design it
- Pro includes 100 credits a month, and Max starts at $200/month
- Credits are consumed by fixing the AI's own mistakes, not just new features


**Pricing:** Pro $20/month (100 credits); Max from $200/month.


**Bottom line:** the closest thing here to "describe an iPhone app, get real SwiftUI back," now at $20 a month.


### 3.[Vibecode](https://www.vibecodeapp.com/) : Best for a Prompt-to-Native App With a Built-In Backend


[Vibecode](https://www.vibecodeapp.com/) builds mobile apps from a prompt with a database and authentication included, and uses a transparent credit model: a dollar of credits buys a dollar of the underlying AI usage, with no markup.


Vibecode homepage, captured September 2026.


**Key features:** prompt-to-app with built-in database and auth; App Store submission from the Plus plan; code download and SSH on Pro; Vibecode Sandbox for free experimentation.


**Free plan (re-checked Sep 24, 2026, per[Vibecode's own plans page](https://www.vibecodeapp.com/docs/getting-started/plans-and-credits) ):** $2.50 in one-time credits and access to premium AI models. Explicitly excluded on free: database, authentication, App Store submission, code download, SSH, and priority support.


**Pros:**


- A transparent, cost-plus credit model instead of an opaque message count
- Database and auth are built in once you're on a paid tier, not bolted on
- Credits roll over rather than resetting to zero


**Cons:**


- The free plan cannot touch a database, submit to the App Store, or export code
- Pro, at $50/month, is where code download and SSH actually unlock
- Vibecode says its own pricing tiers are still experimental and may change


**Pricing:** Plus $20/month, Pro $50/month (code download, SSH), Max $200/month.


**Bottom line:** a real native-app pipeline once you're paying, with unusually honest pricing math.


### 4.[Thunkable](https://thunkable.com/) : Best No-Code Native App Builder for a First Mobile Project


[Thunkable](https://thunkable.com/) is a drag-and-drop, no-code builder for native iOS and Android apps, aimed at people who have never shipped a mobile app before.


Thunkable homepage, captured September 2026.


**Key features:** visual drag-and-drop canvas; AI-assisted screen generation; native compilation for iOS and Android from one project; a component marketplace.


**Free plan (re-checked Sep 24, 2026):** 2,000 AI tokens, 3 public projects, 5 screens per project. Projects on free are public only, and the pricing page lists the first "Live Published App" on the Builder plan.


**Pros:**


- The gentlest learning curve of the no-code native builders here
- AI tokens speed up screen generation without requiring code knowledge
- A real native compiler sits behind the visual canvas


**Cons:**


- 5 screens per project is tight for anything beyond a simple app
- Free projects are public, with no private option
- The $18-19 Accelerator tier adds tokens and a private project but no live published app


**Pricing:** Builder $37/month billed yearly ($59 monthly) for 1 live published app and 50,000 AI tokens. Accelerator, from $18/month, adds tokens and a private project without publishing.


**Bottom line:** a reasonable first stop for a no-code native app, if you're prepared to pay before you publish.


### 5.[Draftbit](https://draftbit.com/) : Best for a React Native App You Can Fully Export


[Draftbit](https://draftbit.com/) is a visual builder over React Native with a Supabase backend built in, and it explicitly supports building alongside Claude Code or OpenAI Codex rather than only its own AI.


Draftbit homepage, captured September 2026.


**Key features:** visual editor over real React Native; built-in Supabase backend; bring-your-own AI subscription or API key; one-click web publishing.


**Free plan (verified Sep 23, 2026):** 5,000 one-time credits, 3 projects, 2 apps per project, 1-click publishing to the web only (draftbit.dev). Code export and native app store publishing are not available on free.


**Pros:**


- The cheapest entry price in this entire list to unlock native publishing: $12/month
- Real React Native output with full code export
- A built-in Supabase backend means no separate database to wire up


**Cons:**


- Free tier is web-only; native publishing is a paid-plan feature
- Only 1 REST API integration per project and 1 sandbox running at a time
- Smaller ecosystem and community than FlutterFlow


**Pricing:** Standard $12/month ($9.60/month billed annually) for code editing, full export, and iOS/Android store publishing.


**Bottom line:** the best cost-per-native-app in this list once you're ready to pay for it.


### 6.[Adalo](https://www.adalo.com/) : Best Visual Builder With Native App Store Publishing


[Adalo](https://www.adalo.com/) is a no-code visual builder with an AI assistant added on top, compiling native iOS IPA files and publishing to both app stores and the web from a single project.


Adalo homepage, captured September 2026.


**Key features:** visual multi-screen canvas; AI assistant for generation; hosted Postgres database; native iOS and Android compilation; web publishing from the same project.


**Free plan (verified Sep 23, 2026):** unlimited test apps, capped at 500 records per app. Publishing to either app store requires a paid plan, and Adalo branding stays on until you upgrade.


**Pros:**


- Unlimited apps in test mode, so you can prototype several ideas at once
- One project reaches iOS, Android, and web without separate builds
- A hosted database is included even on the free plan


**Cons:**


- Nothing you build on free reaches the App Store or Google Play
- Starter, the cheapest publishing tier, is $36/month billed annually
- 500 records per app is a real ceiling for a data-heavy app


**Pricing:** Starter $36/month (billed annually) to publish one app to web and native stores, with custom domain and branding removal included.


**Bottom line:** a mature no-code native option once you accept that testing and publishing are two different price tiers.


### 7.[Bravo Studio](https://www.bravostudio.app/) : Best for Turning a Figma Design Into a Native App


[Bravo Studio](https://www.bravostudio.app/) starts from a Figma file rather than a prompt: you design the screens yourself, and Bravo compiles them into a real native app. Bravo MCP, included on the paid Solo plan, now lets Claude, Cursor, or another AI tool turn Lovable, Pencil, Figma, or Bravo Studio designs into React Native apps.


Bravo homepage, captured September 2026.


**Key features:** Figma-to-native compilation; up to 15 screens on the free Starter tier; a live device previewer; Bravo MCP for AI-assisted building on Solo.


**Free plan (re-checked Sep 24, 2026):** unlimited app projects, up to 15 screens per app, the Bravo Vision previewer, and community support. Publishing to any store requires a paid plan.


**Pros:**


- Designers who already work in Figma get a native app with no new design tool to learn
- Unlimited projects to prototype with on free
- Bravo MCP outputs React Native you own, which Bravo Studio itself does not export


**Cons:**


- You need a finished Figma design before Bravo can do anything, unlike a prompt-first tool
- 15 screens caps what the free tier can represent
- Publishing is entirely paid, starting at $22/month


**Pricing:** Solo $22/month, billed monthly, for unlimited store builds, 30 screens per app, and Bravo MCP.


**Bottom line:** the right choice specifically for teams whose process already starts in Figma.


---


## AI Code Builders That Start in the Browser


These write real app code in a browser tab. Some hand the native build to another service, and one, Replit, now runs a guided App Store flow of its own.


### 8.[Bolt](https://bolt.new/) : Best Free Token Allowance for Scaffolding a React Native App


[Bolt](https://bolt.new/) is StackBlitz's browser-based AI code generator, and its Expo integration, built with Expo directly, scaffolds a real React Native project with routing and styling from a prompt, previewable instantly on your own phone via Expo Go.


**Key features:** prompt-to-code in the browser; Expo starter template for React Native; QR-code preview on a real device through Expo Go; GitHub export.


**Free plan (verified Sep 23, 2026):** 1,000,000 tokens a month with a 300,000-token daily cap — the largest raw free allowance of any tool in this list, mobile or web.


**Pros:**


- By far the most generous free token allowance in this category
- Real, exportable React Native source from the first generation
- Testing on your own phone via Expo Go takes about a minute


**Cons:**


- No native build pipeline of its own — WebContainers cannot run Xcode, Android Studio, or EAS
- No backend, database, or AI agent; a real app means wiring Supabase yourself
- Getting from Bolt's code to a signed IPA or APK requires Expo Application Services or a third-party wrapper


**Pricing:** Pro $25/month for 10M tokens and no daily cap.


**Bottom line:** the best free way to get real React Native code in your hands; budget separately for the native build step that turns it into an install.


### 9.[a0.dev](https://a0.dev/) : Best for One Prompt Aimed at the App Store, Play Store, and Web


[a0.dev](https://a0.dev/) markets prompt-to-app generation that deploys to "App Store, Google Play Store, and web" from one codebase, with a built-in AI coding agent and Convex or Supabase for the database.


**Key features:** one-prompt generation targeting three destinations from a single codebase; built-in database options; integrated payments and an analytics dashboard, per the vendor's own product page.


**Free plan (re-checked Sep 24, 2026):** a0.dev's[pricing page](https://a0.dev/pricing) , read in a headless browser, lists only paid plans. Third-party trackers report a free tier of 1 app project, which we could not confirm on the vendor's own page.


**Pros:**


- Targets all three destinations — both stores and web — from a stated single codebase
- Built-in payments and analytics beyond what most builders on this list include
- A coding-agent approach rather than pure drag-and-drop


**Cons:**


- We could not confirm a free tier on the vendor's own page
- The underlying mobile framework is not disclosed on the marketing site
- Newer and less independently reviewed than FlutterFlow, Adalo, or Thunkable


**Pricing:** Pro $20/month for 100 credits, unlimited app builds, code export, and a custom domain; Max $200/month for 1,250 credits.


**Bottom line:** worth testing given the three-destination claim and the code export on its entry tier, but confirm the free allowance yourself before you plan around it.


### 10.[Replit](https://replit.com/) : Best for a Guided iOS App Store Path From a Browser IDE


[Replit](https://replit.com/) is a browser IDE with an AI agent and hosting built in. Its Agent builds mobile apps in React Native through Expo, and[Replit's mobile docs](https://docs.replit.com/learn/mobile/expo) describe a guided flow from the editor to TestFlight to the App Store. The same docs state that publishing to Google Play is not yet supported.


**Key features:** full cloud IDE; Replit Agent for prompt-to-app generation; iOS Simulator and Android Emulator previews in the editor; Expo Go on a real phone; guided TestFlight and App Store submission.


**Free plan (verified Sep 23, 2026, per[Replit's own billing docs](https://docs.replit.com/billing/plans/replit-core) ):** 1 published app, marked "(30-day)" in Replit's own plan comparison, carrying a "Made with Replit" badge. Agent usage draws on limited daily credits.


**Pros:**


- The best environment here for actually learning to read and fix the generated code
- Hosting and editing live in one place with no separate deploy step
- A real, if credit-metered, AI agent rather than a template picker


**Cons:**


- Google Play publishing is not supported yet, per Replit's own docs
- One published app on free, time-limited and badged
- App Store submission still needs your own Apple Developer Program membership


**Pricing:** Core, from $20/month, for unlimited published apps and badge removal.


**Bottom line:** the best pick here if you want to read and fix the code and still reach the App Store from one browser tab. Plan Android separately.


---


## Spreadsheet- and Workspace-Backed Mobile Tools


These build mobile-responsive apps over data you already have, published as installable web apps rather than native binaries.


### 11.[Glide](https://www.glideapps.com/) : Best for a Spreadsheet-Backed Mobile App


[Glide](https://www.glideapps.com/) turns Google Sheets, Excel, or its own tables into mobile-friendly apps, and remains one of the fastest routes from a spreadsheet to something usable on a phone.


**Key features:** spreadsheet and native table data sources; mobile-responsive output; AI features for building app logic; row-level permissions on paid tiers.


**Free plan (verified Sep 23, 2026):** 10 projects, 2 team members, and a limited credit allowance. The pricing page lists 0 published apps and 0 enabled workflows on Free.


**Pros:**


- Fast path from a spreadsheet you already maintain to a phone-ready interface
- Genuinely mobile-first output with little design work required
- Data stays in a source you already control


**Cons:**


- Publishing itself sits on the paid Basic plan
- Credits on the free tier are limited and vendor-described only as "limited," not a fixed number

FIRST NATIVE LAUNCH, IN ORDER                      TYPICAL WAIT

4. Build and sign the IPA and AAB in your builder  minutes to an hour

6. Submit to App Review                            90% under 24 hours
7. Fix, rebuild, resubmit if rejected              23% of 2025 submissions
8. Apply for Google Play production access         after the 14 days
Mobile-web path: build, publish, share the URL.    minutes

How long does App Store and Google Play review take?


Apple says 90% of submissions are reviewed in under 24 hours on average, and it rejected about 23% of 2025 submissions, each of which restarts the clock.
